note: Figures verified against each state's department of revenue or statute on the retrieved date. Washington is stated under its permanent law for deaths on or after 2026-07-01 (ESB 6347); see wa_first_half_2026 for the earlier regime. Iowa repealed its inheritance tax for deaths after 2024 (S.F. 619) and is therefore absent.

wa_first_half_2026.note: Deaths on or after 2026-01-01 and before 2026-07-01.

jurisdictions.name: Washington
jurisdictions.special_rule: Deaths before 2026-07-01 use a $3,076,000 exclusion and rates up to 35%.

jurisdictions.name: Oregon
jurisdictions.special_rule: Lowest threshold in the country. Tax is computed on the whole taxable estate once the $1,000,000 threshold is crossed.

jurisdictions.name: Illinois
jurisdictions.special_rule: Interrelated calculation under the Attorney General's instructions rather than a simple bracket table. Effective marginal rate just above the threshold is roughly 28%.

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts
jurisdictions.special_rule: Computed from the former federal state death tax credit table (Table A) less a $99,600 credit, which produces the $2,000,000 effective exemption.

jurisdictions.name: Rhode Island
jurisdictions.special_rule: Computed from the former federal credit table (Table A) less an $87,940 credit. Exemption is inflation adjusted annually.

jurisdictions.name: New York
jurisdictions.special_rule: Cliff. The exemption phases out completely once the estate exceeds 105% of the threshold ($7,717,500), and above that point the entire estate is taxed from the first dollar.

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut
jurisdictions.special_rule: Exemption matches the federal basic exclusion. Flat 12%, with total tax capped at $15,000,000. Connecticut is the only state that also levies its own gift tax.

jurisdictions.name: Vermont
jurisdictions.special_rule: Flat 16% on the excess over the exemption.

jurisdictions.name: District of Columbia
jurisdictions.special_rule: Zero bracket amount is inflation adjusted annually.

jurisdictions.name: Maryland
jurisdictions.special_rule: Only jurisdiction with both taxes. 16% estate tax above $5,000,000 plus a 10% inheritance tax on heirs outside close family. The two are credited against each other.

jurisdictions.name: Pennsylvania
jurisdictions.special_rule: Taxed from the first dollar with no exemption. Spouses 0%, children and parents 4.5%, siblings 12%, all others 15%.

jurisdictions.name: New Jersey
jurisdictions.special_rule: Class A (spouse, children, grandchildren, parents) fully exempt. Class C (siblings, children-in-law) 11% to 16% over a $25,000 allowance. Class D (everyone else) 15% to 16% from the first dollar.

jurisdictions.name: Kentucky
jurisdictions.special_rule: Class A (spouse, children, grandchildren, parents, siblings) fully exempt. Class B (nieces, nephews) 4% to 16% over $1,000. Class C (unrelated) 6% to 16% over $500.

jurisdictions.name: Nebraska
jurisdictions.special_rule: Levied at county level per beneficiary. Close relatives 1% over $100,000 each, remote relatives 11% over $40,000, all others 15% over $25,000. Heirs under 22 are exempt.
